findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Trace and state (with a Read of inbound_differ.py:739-767) whether an inbound link-removal record actually reaches G5 (_inbound_unlink_one) in a normal reconcile pass, given G4's same-pass suppression drops it upstream; if G4 suppresses it, correct the premise 're-emits and re-declines on every reconcile pass' and justify why the G5-only fix converges the operator-visible symptom.
evidence: Plan quote: 'The decline is permanent: the removal record re-emits and re-declines on every reconcile pass, so inbound link removal NEVER CONVERGES for a double-related pair.'

inbound_differ.py:739-767 — G4 action-aware same-pass suppression drops inbound remove records whose target key is in link_add_keys|link_remove_keys; comment at :746-755 states 'never mirror a removal for it'.
inbound_differ.py:707 — _diff_link_removals_inbound output is appended to link_mutations, then filtered by the G4 block before an InboundMutation is produced.
apply_inbound_records.py:590-600 — G5 decline lives downstream of compute_inbound_mutations, so it is only reached by remove records G4 did not suppress.

Ticket 2b16 comments (material under review) record a probe: 'compute_inbound_mutations, WITH the outbound link ADD a real bidirectional pass emits -> []' — i.e. the remove is suppressed at G4 before reaching G5.
findings.finding: The plan's load-bearing convergence premise — 'The decline is permanent: the removal record re-emits and re-declines on every reconcile pass, so inbound link removal NEVER CONVERGES for a double-related pair' — is a confident assertion about a runtime path that the codebase contradicts. An inbound {action:'remove'} record reaches G5 (_inbound_unlink_one, apply_inbound_records.py:590-600) only after surviving the G4 same-pass link suppression in compute_inbound_mutations (inbound_differ.py:739-767), which drops the remove whenever the target's peer key is in link_add_keys|link_remove_keys. Per ticket 2b16's own documented+probed refutation, a peer deletion always produces an outbound ADD for that pair, so G4 suppresses the inbound remove upstream and it never reaches the G5 decline in a normal bidirectional pass. The plan neither cites G4 nor establishes how a remove record reaches G5 to 're-decline every pass'.
findings.location: Plan 'Context / Problem' (final sentence: 'The decline is permanent ... NEVER CONVERGES') and 'Approach' step 2 ('the G5 decline case converges')
scenarios: A double-related pair where the peer drops one relation on a normal bidirectional reconcile pass: the outbound differ emits an ADD for the still-local dep, G4 suppresses the inbound remove, and the G5 decline the plan targets is never exercised — so the 'never converges' symptom the plan is built to fix may not manifest via G5 at all.
